multipleChoice.question: What does James say a wise man does when he hears Jesus's words?
options: He teaches them to others
He builds his house on rock
He writes them in a scroll
He prays about them
multipleChoice.explanation: James quotes the parable: the wise man who hears these words and does them is like a man who builds his house on rock.

multipleChoice.question: What happens to the house built on rock when the storm comes?
options: It shakes badly
It does not fall
It falls into the river
It needs to be rebuilt
multipleChoice.explanation: The house built on rock does not fall, because it was founded on rock.

multipleChoice.question: What does Martha compare Peter and Matthew to when she introduces the parable?
options: Seed falling on different soils
Two builders
The sons in a parable of Jesus
Workers who forget their tasks
multipleChoice.explanation: Martha asks James: 'In what parable shall we place our sons?' Then she tells the children a parable of Jesus about two sons.

multipleChoice.question: In the parable of the Growing Seed, who makes the seed sprout and grow?
options: The farmer by his hard work
The rain and the sun together
The earth by itself, automatically
The children who water it
multipleChoice.explanation: The earth produces fruit by itself — automatically — the farmer does not know how.

multipleChoice.question: What does the mustard seed become in the parable?
options: A vine with many branches
A great tree in whose branches birds nest
A field full of wheat
A tall cedar of Lebanon
multipleChoice.explanation: The mustard seed grows into the greatest of garden plants and becomes a tree so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.

multipleChoice.question: In the parable of the Weeds, when does the enemy sow the weeds?
options: During the day while the farmer watches
While the people are sleeping
Before the wheat is planted
After the harvest
multipleChoice.explanation: While the people were sleeping, the enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat.

multipleChoice.question: What does the farmer say to do with the weeds until harvest?
options: Pull them up immediately
Let them grow together with the wheat
Burn them at once
Move them to another field
multipleChoice.explanation: The farmer says: let both grow together until the harvest; at harvest time I will tell the reapers to collect the weeds first and burn them.

multipleChoice.question: What does James say the field represents in the Weeds parable?
options: The synagogue
The world
The kingdom of Israel
The hearts of the disciples
multipleChoice.explanation: James explains that the field is the world, and the good seed are the sons of the kingdom.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Matthew scold Peter when they are eating under the tree?
options: Peter spilled the water
Peter ate Matthew's fruit after claiming he sowed more seed
Peter forgot to feed the donkey
Peter refused to gather the stones
multipleChoice.explanation: Matthew says Peter took only a little seed, much fell on the road, and then Peter ate Matthew's fruit.

multipleChoice.question: What task does James give Matthew after the argument?
options: Gather the small stones from the field
Lead the sheep to the water
Bring bread from the village
Watch over the donkey
multipleChoice.explanation: James tells Matthew to go and lead the sheep to the water.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Peter fail to gather the stones?
options: He does not understand the instruction
He runs to the tree and watches the birds
He falls asleep under the shade
He goes to help Matthew instead
multipleChoice.explanation: Peter eagerly agrees but immediately runs to the tree, sees the birds, and does not bring the stones.

multipleChoice.question: In the first parable Martha tells, what does the first son do after refusing to go to the vineyard?
options: He stays home and sleeps
He later repents and goes
He sends his brother instead
He asks his father to forgive him
multipleChoice.explanation: The first son says 'I do not want to,' but later, repenting, he goes.

multipleChoice.question: In the parable of the Prodigal Son, what does the younger son ask his father for?
options: Permission to travel to another country
The part of the estate that belongs to him
Work in his father's vineyard
A robe and ring as a gift
multipleChoice.explanation: The younger son asks: 'Father, give me the portion of the estate that belongs to me.'

multipleChoice.question: What does the younger son do after spending everything in the far country?
options: He writes a letter to his father
He finds a new master and becomes rich again
He comes to his senses and decides to return to his father
He stays in the far country and keeps working
multipleChoice.explanation: Coming to himself, he says: 'How many hired servants of my father have bread — I am perishing here with hunger. I will go to my father.'

multipleChoice.question: What does the father do when he sees his son returning from far away?
options: He waits at the door and calls the servants
He runs, falls on his neck, and kisses him
He sends the elder son to meet him
He closes the door and will not see him
multipleChoice.explanation: While the son was still far away, the father saw him, loved him greatly, ran, fell on his neck, and was kissing him.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the elder son angry when he returns from the field?
options: His brother took his room
His father never gave him a goat to celebrate, yet kills the fattened calf for his brother
His brother will now inherit more than him
The servants did not tell him his brother had returned
multipleChoice.explanation: The elder son says: 'You never gave me a young goat to celebrate with my friends, but you kill the fattened calf for this son of yours.'

multipleChoice.question: How does Peter's reconciliation with Matthew mirror the Prodigal Son parable?
options: Peter gives Matthew a robe and ring
Peter runs and falls on Matthew's neck, just as the father did in the parable
Matthew goes away and Peter waits for him
James slaughters an animal to celebrate
multipleChoice.explanation: Peter, rejoicing with great joy, runs and falls on Matthew's neck and kisses him — just as the father did in the parable.

trueFalse.statement: The foolish man builds his house on rock.
trueFalse.explanation: The foolish man builds on sand; the wise man builds on rock.

trueFalse.statement: When the storm strikes the house built on sand, it falls with a great crash.
trueFalse.explanation: The house built on sand falls, and its fall is great.

trueFalse.statement: Peter sows a single grain of seed in the field to demonstrate the parable.
trueFalse.explanation: Peter places one small grain in the ground to illustrate how a tiny seed grows into a great plant.

trueFalse.statement: The mustard seed is the largest of all seeds.
trueFalse.explanation: The mustard seed is the smallest of seeds, yet it grows into the greatest plant.

trueFalse.statement: In the Weeds parable, the servants of the householder sowed the weeds.
trueFalse.explanation: An enemy sowed the weeds among the wheat while the people were sleeping.

trueFalse.statement: The righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
trueFalse.explanation: James explains: 'Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.'

trueFalse.statement: James says farming parables are suited to the children because they work in the field.
trueFalse.explanation: James explains that he uses parables from farming because the children work the earth and can understand what they see.

trueFalse.statement: Matthew completes his task willingly when James first assigns it.
trueFalse.explanation: Matthew refuses at first, saying he always leads the animals.

trueFalse.statement: Peter eagerly agrees to gather the stones but never actually does it.
trueFalse.explanation: Peter says 'I will, father!' but immediately runs to the tree and watches the birds instead.

trueFalse.statement: In Martha's first parable, the son who said 'yes' actually did the work.
trueFalse.explanation: The son who said 'yes, lord' did not go; it was the one who first refused but later repented who actually went.

trueFalse.statement: The younger son spent his estate while living in a far country.
trueFalse.explanation: He went to a far country and scattered his estate there, living dissolutely.

trueFalse.statement: The famine that struck the far country helped the younger son find good work.
trueFalse.explanation: The famine made his situation worse; he ended up feeding pigs and wanting to eat what the pigs ate.

trueFalse.statement: The younger son planned to return as a son and ask for his inheritance back.
trueFalse.explanation: He planned to return and say 'I am no longer worthy to be called your son; place me as one of your hired servants.'

trueFalse.statement: The father gave his returning son a robe, a ring, and sandals.
trueFalse.explanation: The father told his servants: bring the best robe and clothe him, give a ring for his hand and sandals for his feet.

trueFalse.statement: The elder son was glad when he heard music and dancing at the house.
trueFalse.explanation: When the elder son heard music and dancing, he inquired what it was and then refused to go in.

trueFalse.statement: James says the father in the parable went out to both sons.
trueFalse.explanation: James teaches: 'The father in the parable did not stay in the house; he went out to both sons.'

trueFalse.statement: Matthew immediately forgives Peter without hesitation.
trueFalse.explanation: Matthew first asks his father: 'Must I forgive him again?' — then, after James says yes, he forgives.

yesNo.question: Does a house built on rock fall when storms come?
yesNo.explanation: The house built on rock does not fall; only the house built on sand falls.

yesNo.question: Is the kingdom of heaven like a mustard seed, according to Jesus?
yesNo.explanation: James says Jesus told the parable: the kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed.

yesNo.question: Does the farmer in the Growing Seed parable understand how the seed sprouts?
yesNo.explanation: The seed sprouts and grows — the farmer does not know how.

yesNo.question: Will the weeds be burned at the harvest?
yesNo.explanation: The weeds are collected at harvest and burned.

yesNo.question: Does Martha bring food and water to the family in the field?
yesNo.explanation: Martha and Magdalene come from the village and place bread, water, and honey in the shade for the family.

yesNo.question: In the first parable, does the son who said 'I will go' actually go?
yesNo.explanation: The son who said 'Yes, lord' did not go; the one who said 'I do not want to' later repented and went.

yesNo.question: Did the younger son's father see him while he was still far away?
yesNo.explanation: While he was still far away, his father saw him and loved him greatly.

yesNo.question: Was the elder son happy that his brother had returned?
yesNo.explanation: The elder son was angry and refused to enter the house.

yesNo.question: Does Peter confess to Matthew that he was wrong?
yesNo.explanation: Peter goes to Matthew and says: 'I sinned against you; I bit you and ate your fruit — forgive me.'

yesNo.question: Does James say that God has mercy on us, just as the father in the parable?
yesNo.explanation: James teaches: 'Such is God — he is good and faithful and has mercy on us. As your Father in heaven has mercy on you, so also have mercy on one another.'

yesNo.question: Do Peter and Matthew return home as enemies?
yesNo.explanation: Having become friends again and forgetting their wrongs, the two brothers walk together on the road to the village.
